name: Schloss Itter
kurzbeschreibung: Historic Itter Castle crowns a prominent rocky knoll at the entrance of the Brixental valley and gained worldwide fame for its 1945 battle.
beschreibung:
Overview

The storied Itter Castle (Schloss Itter) commands a prominent, densely wooded rocky knoll above the village of Itter at the scenic entrance to the Brixental valley. Visible from afar, the fortified stronghold overlooks the rolling green pastures of the Kitzbühel Alps and looks back upon more than seven hundred years of eventful history. Originally established in the 13th century by the Prince-Bishops of Regensburg as a frontier fortress against Tyrol, the castle passed through diverse noble hands before being refurbished in romantic historicist style during the late 19th century. The estate gained worldwide historical renown during the dramatic Battle of Castle Itter on May 5, 1945, an extraordinary cooperative defense at the end of World War II.

Route & Requirements

The castle compound impresses with fortified medieval architecture featuring circular stone turrets, steeply pitched tiled roofs, oriels, battlements, and sturdy defensive curtain walls. Because the estate is privately owned, the castle interior is closed to the public. However, a delightful and sunny panoramic walking circuit encircles the entire castle rock, offering wonderful vistas of the architecture from changing vantage points. Informative educational signs along the footpath recount the building's historical phases and the historic 1945 battle, when American soldiers, Wehrmacht officers, and Austrian resistance fighters defended prominent French dignitaries against Waffen-SS troops. The trail requires only comfortable walking shoes and provides inviting benches.

Visit & Arrival

The scenic loop trail around Itter Castle and panoramic viewpoints in the village are accessible year-round free of charge. Arrival by car: take the Inntal autobahn A12 to exit Wörgl Ost, turn onto the B178 federal highway towards Kitzbühel, and follow signs to Itter. Free public parking is available in the village center near the parish church or at the Salvistabahn cable car station. By public transit: take the train to Wörgl Hauptbahnhof or Hopfgarten im Brixental, followed by regional VVT bus connections running regularly directly to the Itter Dorf stop.

Tips

Combine your castle walk with a stroll along the renowned Itterer Rosenweg (Rose Trail), which showcases hundreds of lovingly tended rosebushes and tranquil benches throughout this sunny village. On clear days, the Kirchbichler viewpoint affords breathtaking panoramas across the Inn Valley towards the jagged limestone summits of the Kaiser Mountains and Hohe Salve. In the village, traditional Tyrolean inns invite you to savor warm local hospitality and delicious regional specialties.
preis: Exterior areas and perimeter trail free of charge (castle interior is private)
oeffnungszeiten: Exteriors and panoramic perimeter trails accessible freely year-round
